title: The MettleUp access card can say 'MettleUp has never opened your records' when it did, more than 2 years ago
what: The owner's MettleUp access card shows 'MettleUp has never opened your records' whenever its list is empty. The list only holds support windows and MettleUp actions from the last 2 years, and the nightly clean-up deletes older ones. So a gym whose records were opened more than 2 years ago is told they were never opened. The sentence also ignores direct database looks, which the card never reads (already written as a separate finding).
expected: The empty line says what is true, for example 'MettleUp has not opened your records in the last 2 years', matching the 2-year keep time in the privacy notice.
how_often: only for gyms whose last support look is over 2 years old
fix_line: Change the empty-list sentence to say 'in the last 2 years' (and count direct looks once the card shows them).

items.reason: All 7 listed promises read in code. P-A7-panel-3-02 (only when you let them) and P-A7-panel-3-01 (only totals, never a name): broken by MettleUp's emergency door that opens a gym's records without the owner, already FN-A5-server-database-1-3-01; direct database looks not shown, already FN-A3-notes-claude-1-01. P-A7-panel-3-03 (never opened): new finding 01 for the 2-year window, plus the direct-look gap above. P-A7-panel-3-05 (delete within 30 days, call first): the button only sends a request to MettleUp's feedback box, which HQ lists and turns into a tracked request; the call step is enforced, the 30-day reminder gap is already FN-L4-hq-app-06, leftovers after a delete already FN-L4-hq-app-03 and -05. P-A7-panel-3-34 (pay on the payment company's page): the page is the payment company's own link, but the owner's name and mobile go to it without the notice naming it for this, already FN-L4-server-hq-gate-workers-02 (feature hidden, test mode). P-A7-panel-3-35: a counting note, no personal data; the copy says what the counting does. P-A7-panel-3-40: kept; removing a refused desk item only drops it from this device's outbox, owner only, after a confirm.

DPDP duties that touch this area: the notice of who can see gym data (the access card) is contradicted by the emergency door, already FN-A5-server-database-1-3-01; erasing a whole gym is a request with a call-back and a 30-day promise, reminder gap already FN-L4-hq-app-06. Terms acceptance and consent live in the sign-in area, not here. No children's data, no breach handling and no consent screens in this area. The desk photo sheet tells staff who sees the photo.

The access card lists support windows (both doors, with who opened it and why), each look with what and how many rows, and MettleUp actions, from the server's owner access answer. It never reads the server's list of direct database looks, already FN-A3-notes-claude-1-01; the 'never opened' line can be wrong after 2 years (01).

This area keeps no personal data in the browser: its local and session storage hold only display choices, dismissals, the last download day and quick-action picks. Gym delete: the 30-day promise is not reminded in HQ, already FN-L4-hq-app-06. Support-look records are kept 2 years as the notice says. The desk's offline copy and unsent work belong to the data area, already written there.

Outside sends from this area: MettleUp plan checkout sends the owner's name and mobile to Razorpay or Cashfree, not named for this in the notice, already FN-L4-server-hq-gate-workers-02 (hidden, test mode). Alerts with the app closed go by web push encrypted for the one browser, so the browser's push company cannot read the line. The member card and the new-gym share use the device's own WhatsApp or share sheet; MettleUp sends nothing. No AI, analytics, Health Connect, Google Health or Fitbit calls in this area.

The only delete in this area is 'Delete our gym from MettleUp': it sends a request (nothing is deleted from the button), and HQ must call the gym before its delete runs. What that delete misses is already written: page photos (FN-L4-hq-app-03), the second database (FN-L4-hq-app-05). Nightly backups expire by themselves, per the HQ audit. A real delete was not run (live write).
